title: Cooling Tower Gearbox
model_title: Cooling Tower Gearbox — Right-Angle Spiral-Bevel + Helical Reducer (≈ 10:1)

introduction.definition: A cooling tower gearbox is a right-angle reducer between the motor drive shaft and the fan. A spiral-bevel gear set turns the drive through 90° and a helical stage completes about a 10:1 reduction to the vertical output shaft, which carries the fan hub and its thrust. Gears dip in an oil bath that splash-lubricates the bearings.
applications: Air-cooled condenser and large agitator drives (similar right-angle reducers)
key_points: Remote oil gauge and fill outside the stack
introduction.summary: A cooling tower gearbox is a right-angle speed reducer. A spiral-bevel gear set turns the horizontal drive through 90° and a helical stage completes about a 10:1 reduction to the vertical fan shaft. It is splash-lubricated from an oil bath and designed for a wet, cycling environment.

pressure.title: Speed down, torque up
pressure.description: Motor speed (≈ 1500 rpm) is reduced about 10:1 to fan speed (≈ 150 rpm): the spiral-bevel set (40/12 ≈ 3.3) turns the drive through 90° and the helical set (45/15 = 3) completes the reduction. Output torque ≈ input torque × ratio × efficiency, so the output shaft and its bearings are much heavier. Gearboxes are selected with a service factor (typically ≥ 2.0 for cooling-tower duty), run in a humid, often icing environment, and depend on correct oil level — hence the remote oil gauge outside the stack.

video_tutorials.title: Cooling Tower Gearbox — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Cooling Tower Gearbox.
A cooling tower gearbox is a right-angle reducer between the motor drive shaft and the fan.
A spiral-bevel gear set turns the drive through 90° and a helical stage completes about a 10:1 reduction to the vertical output shaft, which carries the fan hub and its thrust.
Gears dip in an oil bath that splash-lubricates the bearings.
Typical applications include cooling tower fans; air-cooled condenser and large agitator drives (similar right-angle reducers).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Gear Housing (cast iron, split in cutaway) with Mounting Flange, Input Shaft & Spiral-Bevel Pinion (z = 12) with Coupling Hub, Intermediate Shaft: Spiral-Bevel Gear (z = 40) & Helical Pinion (z = 15), Vertical Output Shaft & Helical Gear (z = 45) with Fan-Hub Flange.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Cooling Tower Gearbox works.
Input shaft and pinion turn at motor speed.
The bevel gear turns the drive 90°.
The helical stage reduces speed further.
Gears dip in oil that splashes onto bearings.
The output shaft carries the fan.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Motor speed (≈ 1500 rpm) is reduced about 10:1 to fan speed (≈ 150 rpm): the spiral-bevel set (40/12 ≈ 3.3) turns the drive through 90° and the helical set (45/15 = 3) completes the reduction.

video_tutorials.title: Cooling Tower Gearbox — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Cooling Tower Gearbox.
Check remote oil level and vibration.
Oil analysis (water!).
Inspect gear contact; replace bearings/seals.
Watch for water in oil: milky oil, rust. Common cause: breather/seal failure.
Watch for bearing failure: noise, heat, vibration. Common cause: low oil, contamination.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
